findings.title: OpenStreetMap — Busan Station full tag+geometry extract (Overpass), incl. indoor-mapping census
findings.whatItShows: 348 features in the station bbox. HARD COUNT: indoor=* features = 2, and BOTH are amenity=luggage_locker NODES (indoor=yes). Ways/relations carrying indoor=* = 0. indoor in {room,corridor,wall,area,level} = 0. room=* = 0. level=* = 11, all POI nodes (shops/cafes), zero level-tagged geometry. Positive geometry that DOES exist: building=train_station way 165346389 (63 pts, building:levels=3, 352.4m N-S x 253.4m E-W = whole complex incl. train shed), building=train_station way 165346394 (29 pts, amenity=public_building, 45.3m x 84.2m = 역사 proper), building:part ways 1305717763 (44 pts, 139.8x87.1m) and 1554396381, 6 railway=platform ways, 2 railway=train_station_entrance nodes, 2 highway=elevator, 3 building=roof (canopies).
findings.usefulFor: DEFINITIVE NEGATIVE on OSM indoor mapping: there is no indoor room/wall/corridor polygon for Busan Station anywhere in OSM, so no OSM-derived interior can be imported. The POSITIVE value is the exported GeoJSON footprint: georeferenced outer shell + platform + canopy polygons to georeference/validate the existing OfficialBusanStation_MainShell.fbx and to place platform-access gates on the correct side.

findings.title: Rotation-corrected true footprints of every OSM polygon, in metres (derived) — resolves the FBX/OSM georeference conflict
findings.whatItShows: Minimum-area enclosing rectangles computed by rotating calipers in a local ENU frame. Two near-orthogonal orientation families: 역사 head-house at bearing 162.0 deg CCW-from-East (compass 108.0) and platforms/train shed at 69.6 deg (compass 20.4). The ACUTE angle between them is 87.6 deg, not 90 - the head-house is 2.4 deg off square to the tracks, worth 3.38 m of drift over its 80.6 m run, so rotation must be measured, never derived as platforms+90. Key rectangles: way/165346394 (역사 head-house) 80.6 x 31.5 m = 2537 m2 @162.0 deg; way/165346389 (whole complex) 372.4 x 180.5 m @160.8 deg; way/1305717763 132.6 x 57.6 m @69.8 deg; five platforms 389-461 m long, refs 1 / 3;4 / 5;6 / 8;9 / 10;11. The previously circulated 352x253 and 45x84 figures were lat-lon AXIS-ALIGNED bounding boxes of a building rotated ~19 deg off north, so they were never footprints and were not comparable to the Unity AABB of 98x63.
findings.usefulFor: Makes the georeference decidable. The 역사 head-house footprint is 2537 m2; the reported 2F 대합실 usable area of 1820-1992 m2 is 72-79% of that, a normal concourse net-to-gross, which independently corroborates that way/165346394 is the block the existing FBX interior volume belongs to. Fit the FBX to that 80.6 x 31.5 m rectangle at bearing 162.0 deg about 35.1157262,129.0399028 rather than by comparing extents. Bearings are CCW-from-East mod 180; compass = (90-bearing) mod 180. The platform family at 69.6 deg (compass 20.4) fixes which facade the platform-access gates must pierce, and the recovered platform refs (5 platforms) match namuwiki's 5면 12선.

findings.title: 한국철도공사_역사내외부 시설현황 (KORAIL station interior/exterior facility census, 2024-12-31)
findings.whatItShows: CSV, 288 KORAIL stations, CP949. Row '부산' gives HARD COUNTS for Busan Station: 엘리베이터 13, 에스컬레이터 24, 휠체어리프트 0, 장애인경사로 0, 장애인화장실 1, 일반화장실 1, 모유수유실 0, 종합안내소 0, 환승주차장 688면. Columns: 역명,엘리베이터,에스컬레이터,휠체어리프트,장애인경사로,장애인화장실,일반화장실,모유수유실,종합안내소,환승주차장(면수).
findings.usefulFor: Directly fixes the vertical-circulation budget for the interior build: exactly 13 elevator shafts and 24 escalator runs must be placed across the station, 1 accessible WC + 1 general WC block. Turns 'how many escalators?' from invention into a sourced constraint. NOTE the 모유수유실=0 / 종합안내소=0 entries contradict on-site signage lists, so treat the zero-valued columns as 'not recorded in this dataset', not as proven absence.
findings.license: KOGL Type 1 (공공누리 제1유형) — 한국철도공사; free use incl. commercial, attribution required

findings.title: OpenBVE '부산 도시철도 1호선' route package (해산강제작소) — DOWNLOADED AND INSPECTED, NEGATIVE
findings.whatItShows: 544,549,043-byte ZIP pulled anonymously from the author's public Google Drive link (no login). 3,282 entries, CP949 filenames: 1,133 .csv objects, 1,002 .bmp, 387 .png, 256 .wav, 158 .animated, 97 .b3d, 86 .jpg; 2,486 files under Railway/Object/BUSAN1/. I decoded and searched it: ZERO filenames contain '부산역', the route file contains ZERO .Sta directives, and '부산역' appears exactly once in 부산도시철도 1호선.csv as a ';' comment marking chainage. The objects placed at that marker are generic modular trackbed parts only (Busan1\\Ballast*.csv, DarkSlab*.csv, RoadL/RoadR.csv, Formwall*.csv, Null.csv) reused identically at every station on the line.
findings.usefulFor: NOTHING for this build — and that is the point of downloading it. It proves the most-cited Korean BVE '부산역' lead contains no bespoke Busan Station geometry at all, only generic reused tunnel/trackbed modules, and it models the UNDERGROUND Line-1 subway station rather than the above-ground KTX 역사 that CHOOGuard needs. Do not spend a human on this file. The remaining BVE leads (경부고속선/경부선 on Naver Cafe) are a different codebase and remain unverified, but this result lowers the prior on them substantially.
findings.license: Korean hobbyist add-on; post states no redistribution/commercial use without author permission. Recorded as metadata per instruction; not a filter for this research phase.

findings.title: V-World 3차원 시설물 (LoD4 / LoD3 / LoD1) + XDServer3d tile endpoint
findings.whatItShows: V-World's national 3D facility dataset. LoD4 metadata: 데이터 종류 '3D Model', 데이터 포맷 '3ds, jpg', built by 5-direction aerial photogrammetry. Portal 유형 is '지도조회' (map-view) — there is NO bulk download button; access is via the XDWorld 3D tile server, which I probed live: it responds (ERROR_DB_GENERAL for a bogus key, ERROR_SERVICE_PARAMETER_NG without one), so the endpoint is real and only an API key is missing. CRITICAL CAVEAT: Korean 「3차원 국토공간정보 구축작업 규정」 별첨5 defines LoD4 as realistic photo-texture on the EXTERIOR shell — it is NOT CityGML LoD4 and contains NO interior geometry. LoD3 is 대구광역시 only; LoD1 is nationwide extruded footprints (shp).
findings.usefulFor: Exterior-only. Worth exactly one thing: cross-checking the existing FBX shell's massing/height against the national dataset. Do NOT expect interior partitions from V-World. The API key is free but requires a V-World account (Korean real-name/social login), so it is login-walled.
findings.license: 공공누리 / V-World terms; API key required (free registration)

findings.title: 한국철도공사 편의시설정보 / 임대매장정보 Open APIs (tenant + amenity inventory per station)
findings.whatItShows: Two live KORAIL open APIs: per-station convenience-facility records and per-station rental/tenant store records. Confirmed present on data.go.kr; both are 오픈API requiring a data.go.kr service key (활용신청), which requires account login.
findings.usefulFor: 임대매장정보 is the best available substitute for a tenant plan: it should enumerate the actual shops occupying the 대합실 retail bays (편의점/베이커리/올리브영/카페 etc.) so the retail partitions are populated from the real tenant roster rather than guessed. Highest-value login-walled item in this lane after the drawings.
findings.license: KOGL Type 1 — 한국철도공사; requires data.go.kr key

findings.title: openBVE 경부고속선 (서울역/수서역–부산역, 양평, 2024-06-02) and 경부선 (서울역–부산역, dger, 2024-12-14)
findings.whatItShows: The two actively-maintained Korean BVE routes that terminate AT Busan Station. Distribution is inside Naver Cafe 'Metro Phics' (skyrailway, clubId 22319550). I fetched both post URLs anonymously: HTTP 200 but the body is the cafe login shell with g_sUserId="" — the attachment is behind Naver login + cafe membership. Mapped from the namu.wiki table by byte-offset correlation (the 링크 anchors are JS-rendered, so I matched URL positions against the route-name positions).
findings.usefulFor: BVE routes model the trackside world: platforms, canopies, platform furniture, station-building facade as seen from the track, and (for terminus stations) often the platform-level concourse. They do NOT model 2F 대합실 interiors. Realistic value = platform-level geometry and platform-access gate positions, not the 대합실 subdivision. Needs a human with a Naver account.
findings.license: Korean hobbyist add-on, author-restricted redistribution; Naver Cafe membership required

8 API query variants ('busan station', '부산역', 'busan train station', 'ktx station', 'busan', 'korea station', 'korea train station interior', 'railway station interior'): zero Busan Station models. '부산역' returns 0 results outright.
12 query variants incl. 부산역/부산역사/Busan Station/Korail/KTX/경부선. Korean rail modellers have uploaded 서울역, 수원역, 평택역, 오송역(구역사), 함백역 — but no 부산역. Confirmed absence.

7 query variants (busan station 3d, korail station, bve 경부선, openbve korea, bve korail, 부산역). total_count 0 for every 3D/BVE-related query; the only 'busan station' hits are transit ridership data-analysis repos with no geometry.

All three bot-blocked anonymous requests (HTTP 202 empty, 403, 403). Not searchable via curl. Given Sketchfab and 3D Warehouse both returned nothing, a purpose-built commercial Busan Station model is very unlikely; deprioritised rather than confirmed absent.

No 실내공간정보 / indoor-spatial-information product surfaced on NGII's platform (lxIndoorList.do is 404; main page contains zero '실내' mentions). Korea has no public national indoor dataset covering Busan Station.
Searched 'BIM' across 100 results: only 서울주택도시공사 한옥 BIM and LH 토목 BIM 지침. No 국가철도공단/KORAIL railway BIM object library published. No off-the-shelf BIM gates/escalators/platform furniture to reuse.

deadEnds.why: Inspected in full: 0 filenames matching 부산역, 0 .Sta directives, 부산역 present only as a ';' chainage comment, and only generic ballast/slab/road/formwall modules placed there. Contains no Busan Station geometry, and is the subway station, not the KTX 역사.

bestThreeForGeometry: 1. 한국철도공사_역사내외부 시설현황 CSV (ON DISK, KOGL-1, no login) — the only source in this lane that hands you hard interior numbers for Busan specifically: 13 elevators, 24 escalators, 1 accessible WC, 1 general WC. This converts the single most expensive guess in the interior build (how much vertical circulation to place, and therefore where the floor plates must be pierced) into a sourced constraint.

2. osm_footprint_obb_metres.json + busanstation_osm_footprint.geojson (ON DISK, ODbL, no login) — rotation-corrected true footprints plus the georeferenced polygons they came from. Gives the 역사 head-house as 80.6 x 31.5 m = 2537 m2 at bearing 162.0 deg (corroborated by the 1820-1992 m2 2F concourse sitting at 72-79% net-to-gross), the orthogonal platform family at 69.6 deg that fixes which facade the gates pierce, and platform refs 1/3;4/5;6/8;9/10;11. Converts the FBX georeference from a judgement call into a fit.

3. 한국철도공사_임대매장정보 Open API (https://www.data.go.kr/data/15125773/openapi.do, login-walled, free key) — the real tenant roster per station. It is the only identified source that can populate the 대합실 retail bays (편의점/베이커리/카페/올리브영 etc.) from the actual occupancy list rather than invention, and it pairs with 편의시설정보 (15125774) for the amenity rooms. Worth a human spending five minutes on a data.go.kr 활용신청.
